name: Amaziah the priest of Bethel
charge: Forbidding Amos to prophesy at the king’s chapel; sending to Jeroboam that Amos had conspired against him
summary: When Amos, a herdman of Tekoa, prophesied at Bethel that the sanctuaries of Israel would be laid waste and the Lord would rise against the house of Jeroboam with the sword, Amaziah the priest of Bethel sent to King Jeroboam that Amos had conspired against him and the land could not bear his words (Amos 7:7-11). He told the prophet to go and prophesy in Judah and never again at Bethel, the king’s chapel (Amos 7:12-13). Amos answered that the Lord had taken him from the flock to prophesy to Israel, and pronounced the judgment on Amaziah’s house and on Israel’s land (Amos 7:14-17).
offenseFull: Amos prophesied in the days of Uzziah king of Judah and Jeroboam the son of Joash king of Israel (Amos 1:1). History in the AM stresses that this is Jeroboam the second, not Jeroboam the son of Nebat of the split, though he departed not from the sins of the first Jeroboam, who made Israel to sin (2 Kings 14:23-24). The Lord showed Amos grasshoppers eating the grass of the land and a fire devouring the great deep, and twice Amos pleaded for Jacob because he was small, and the Lord relented (Amos 7:1-6). Then the Lord stood on a wall with a plumbline in His hand, a builder’s instrument for measuring, and said He would set it in the midst of His people Israel and not pass by them any more: the high places of Isaac would be desolate, the sanctuaries of Israel laid waste, and He would rise against the house of Jeroboam with the sword (Amos 7:7-9).

Then Amaziah the priest of Bethel, where Jeroboam the son of Nebat had set his calf, sent to the king that Amos had conspired against him in the midst of Israel and the land could not bear all his words, for Amos was saying that Jeroboam would die by the sword and Israel would surely be led away captive out of their land (Amos 7:10-11). The teachers read the report two ways. One class takes it as Amos’s own directness and fearlessness, telling a king to his face that he would die. History in the AM, on the reign of Jeroboam the second, says Amaziah was saucing it up to slander him to the king: Amos had not said Jeroboam would die by the sword, but that the northern kingdom would go into captivity if it did not repent. Either way, the priest tried to put a charge of treason on the prophet to get him put to death. Our own people will do this to us; the time comes when whoever kills you will think he does God service (John 16:2).

Amaziah also told Amos, calling him a seer, to flee into the land of Judah, eat bread and prophesy there, and never prophesy again at Bethel, for it was the king’s chapel and the king’s court (Amos 7:12-13). The class of 2026-07-18 draws the point: Amaziah was more concerned with protecting the king’s institution than with hearing the word of the Lord, and the same thing goes on today. Instead of correcting leaders and teachers with their ridiculous doctrines, they prefer that we not speak at all. It was the northern kingdom’s habit from the beginning: they gave the Nazarites wine to drink and commanded the prophets not to prophesy (Amos 2:11-12), and that goes into lies and deceit, doing anything to stop the word of the Most High.
judgmentFull: Amos answered that he was no prophet and no prophet’s son, but a herdman and a gatherer of sycamore fruit, and the Lord took him as he followed the flock and told him to go and prophesy to His people Israel (Amos 7:14-15). The prophet did not choose himself; the Lord chose him and ordained him, as He ordained Jeremiah before he was born (Jeremiah 1:5). The Most High gives His word to the prophets, and the prophet’s job is to carry out the word of the Lord, no more, no less; if you do not like it, too bad.

Because Amaziah said not to prophesy against Israel nor drop a word against the house of Isaac, the Lord said his wife would be a harlot in the city, his sons and daughters would fall by the sword, his land would be divided by line, he would die in a polluted land, and Israel would surely go into captivity out of its land (Amos 7:16-17). Amaziah was trying to get the brother to stop prophesying, and judgment came on him for that. The priest of the king’s chapel could protect none of it: not his wife, his children, his inheritance, nor the ground he would be buried in. The judgment came as spoken. Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria took Gilead, Galilee and all the land of Naphtali and carried them captive, and in the ninth year of Hoshea Samaria fell and Israel was carried away to Assyria (2 Kings 15:29; 2 Kings 17:6). They did not want to hear it, but it happened, because they sold the righteous for silver and the poor for a pair of shoes, and in that day the mighty would not deliver himself (Amos 2:6; Amos 2:14).

text.text: Thus he shewed me: and, behold, the Lord stood upon a wall made by a plumbline, with a plumbline in his hand.
And the Lord said unto me, Amos, what seest thou? And I said, A plumbline. Then said the Lord, Behold, I will set a plumbline in the midst of my people Israel: I will not again pass by them any more:
And the high places of Isaac shall be desolate, and the sanctuaries of Israel shall be laid waste; and I will rise against the house of Jeroboam with the sword.
Then Amaziah the priest of Beth–el sent to Jeroboam king of Israel, saying, Amos hath conspired against thee in the midst of the house of Israel: the land is not able to bear all his words.
For thus Amos saith, Jeroboam shall die by the sword, and Israel shall surely be led away captive out of their own land.
Also Amaziah said unto Amos, O thou seer, go, flee thee away into the land of Judah, and there eat bread, and prophesy there:
But prophesy not again any more at Beth–el: for it is the king’s chapel, and it is the king’s court.
Then answered Amos, and said to Amaziah, I was no prophet, neither was I a prophet’s son; but I was an herdman, and a gatherer of sycomore fruit:
And the Lord took me as I followed the flock, and the Lord said unto me, Go, prophesy unto my people Israel.
Now therefore hear thou the word of the Lord: Thou sayest, Prophesy not against Israel, and drop not thy word against the house of Isaac.

Therefore thus saith the Lord; Thy wife shall be an harlot in the city, and thy sons and thy daughters shall fall by the sword, and thy land shall be divided by line; and thou shalt die in a polluted land: and Israel shall surely go into captivity forth of his land.

The words of Amos, who was among the herdmen of Tekoa, which he saw concerning Israel in the days of Uzziah king of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joash king of Israel, two years before the earthquake.
In the fifteenth year of Amaziah the son of Joash king of Judah Jeroboam the son of Joash king of Israel began to reign in Samaria, and reigned forty and one years.
And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord: he departed not from all the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin.
Thus hath the Lord God shewed unto me; and, behold, he formed grasshoppers in the beginning of the shooting up of the latter growth; and, lo, it was the latter growth after the king’s mowings.
And it came to pass, that when they had made an end of eating the grass of the land, then I said, O Lord God, forgive, I beseech thee: by whom shall Jacob arise? for he is small.
The Lord repented for this: It shall not be, saith the Lord.
Thus hath the Lord God shewed unto me: and, behold, the Lord God called to contend by fire, and it devoured the great deep, and did eat up a part.
Then said I, O Lord God, cease, I beseech thee: by whom shall Jacob arise? for he is small.
The Lord repented for this: This also shall not be, saith the Lord God.
Thus he shewed me: and, behold, the Lord stood upon a wall made by a plumbline, with a plumbline in his hand.
And the Lord said unto me, Amos, what seest thou? And I said, A plumbline. Then said the Lord, Behold, I will set a plumbline in the midst of my people Israel: I will not again pass by them any more:
And the high places of Isaac shall be desolate, and the sanctuaries of Israel shall be laid waste; and I will rise against the house of Jeroboam with the sword.
Then Amaziah the priest of Beth–el sent to Jeroboam king of Israel, saying, Amos hath conspired against thee in the midst of the house of Israel: the land is not able to bear all his words.
For thus Amos saith, Jeroboam shall die by the sword, and Israel shall surely be led away captive out of their own land.
They shall put you out of the synagogues: yea, the time cometh, that whosoever killeth you will think that he doeth God service.
And I raised up of your sons for prophets, and of your young men for Nazarites. Is it not even thus, O ye children of Israel? saith the Lord.
But ye gave the Nazarites wine to drink; and commanded the prophets, saying, Prophesy not.
Then answered Amos, and said to Amaziah, I was no prophet, neither was I a prophet’s son; but I was an herdman, and a gatherer of sycomore fruit:
And the Lord took me as I followed the flock, and the Lord said unto me, Go, prophesy unto my people Israel.
Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee; and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee, and I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations.
Now therefore hear thou the word of the Lord: Thou sayest, Prophesy not against Israel, and drop not thy word against the house of Isaac.

Therefore thus saith the Lord; Thy wife shall be an harlot in the city, and thy sons and thy daughters shall fall by the sword, and thy land shall be divided by line; and thou shalt die in a polluted land: and Israel shall surely go into captivity forth of his land.

In the days of Pekah king of Israel came Tiglath–pileser king of Assyria, and took Ijon, and Abel–beth–maachah, and Janoah, and Kedesh, and Hazor, and Gilead, and Galilee, all the land of Naphtali, and carried them captive to Assyria.
In the ninth year of Hoshea the king of Assyria took Samaria, and carried Israel away into Assyria, and placed them in Halah and in Habor by the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes.
Thus saith the Lord; For three transgressions of Israel, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because they sold the righteous for silver, and the poor for a pair of shoes;
Therefore the flight shall perish from the swift, and the strong shall not strengthen his force, neither shall the mighty deliver himself:

Thus he shewed me: and, behold, the Lord stood upon a wall made by a plumbline, with a plumbline in his hand.
And the Lord said unto me, Amos, what seest thou? And I said, A plumbline. Then said the Lord, Behold, I will set a plumbline in the midst of my people Israel: I will not again pass by them any more:
And the high places of Isaac shall be desolate, and the sanctuaries of Israel shall be laid waste; and I will rise against the house of Jeroboam with the sword.
But ye gave the Nazarites wine to drink; and commanded the prophets, saying, Prophesy not.
Until the Lord removed Israel out of his sight, as he had said by all his servants the prophets. So was Israel carried away out of their own land to Assyria unto this day.
